title: Prepositional 6: Mixed Review
description: Synthesis. Mixes в, на, о, об across all genders, including the -ия → -ии pattern from L1.
descriptionRussian: Итоговый урок. Смешивает в, на, о, об во всех родах.
intro: Four different words send a noun into this case, and every one of them produces the same endings. That is the useful thing about it: the hard part was never the form, it was noticing that a trigger had fired. Today all four turn up mixed together, so spotting the trigger is the only work left.
rules: Four prepositional triggers learned: в (location: building/enclosed/city), на (location: surface/event/idiomatic), о (topic, before consonant), об (topic, before vowel а/и/о/у/э).
Form rules in one place: masc + -е, fem -а → -е, fem -я → -е, neuter -о → -е, fem -ия → -ии (Lesson 1). The same forms apply after any of the four prepositional triggers.
Identify the trigger first, then apply the gender rule. Same noun behaves differently depending on the trigger and on its ending.
examples: Книга на столе. (location, на, masc cons)
Я думаю о маме. (topic, о, fem -а)
Антон знает об Иване. (topic, об, masc vowel)
Они в России. (location, в, fem -ия NEW)

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 4: о + fem -а becomes...?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 4: о + fem -а changes -а to -е. Мама → о маме. The case form is the same after о, в, and на.

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 1: masculine consonant + 'в' takes...?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 1: в + masculine consonant adds -е. Магазин → в магазине. After all four prepositional triggers (в, на, о, об), the case form follows the same gender rules.

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 3: 'на работе' is the standard form. What's the case ending?
items.explanation: Russian uses 'на работе' (idiomatic на). The case form follows the fem -а → -е pattern. Работа → работе.

items.promptEnglish: Lena is writing about the film.
items.hint: О triggers prepositional. Фильм is masculine consonant.
items.explanation: О triggers prepositional just like в and на. Фильм is masculine consonant: + -е → фильме.

items.hint: Антон starts with а (vowel). The preposition is 'об'; what's the case form?
items.explanation: Антон starts with а (vowel), so the preposition is 'об' (the 'б' is added for pronunciation). The case form is the standard masculine + -е: Антон → Антоне.

items.hint: Россия ends in -ия. This is a special pattern: -ия → -ии.
items.explanation: Россия ends in -ия. This is a special soft-stem pattern: -ия → -ии in the prepositional case. Россия → в России. The same -ия → -ии pattern works for лекция (на лекции), история (об истории), and other -ия nouns.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Иван is masculine consonant. After 'об' (topic + vowel-initial), prepositional adds -е → Иване.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The tourists are in Italy now.
errorCorrection.explanation: Italy's name ends in -ия, and -ия nouns take -ии in the prepositional, not -е: в Италии. Италие is the trap a learner makes by applying the regular -е ending; the -ия subset blocks it. The same -ии pattern covers в России, в Англии, на лекции.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The doctors work at the hospital.
errorCorrection.explanation: Больница is a building, so location takes в: в больнице. На больнице would put the action on the roof. The в/на split sends buildings and enclosed places to в (в больнице, в школе, в офисе) and surfaces and event places to на (на столе, на работе).

Ольга starts with the vowel О, so the topic preposition is об, not о: об Ольге. Plain о would leave two vowels colliding. The noun stays in the prepositional, with the regular fem -а → -е ending: Ольге.

minimalPairs.explanation: After 'в' (location), the noun shifts to the prepositional case: магазине. The nominative магазин would be a subject: 'Магазин закрыт' (The store is closed).
Россия ends in -ия. The prepositional form is России (-ия → -ии). Compare with regular fem -а: Москва → Москве. The -ия subset has its own special ending.

patternRecognition.question: What kind of preposition usage is this?
options: на for events and idiomatic places
patternRecognition.answer: на for events and idiomatic places
patternRecognition.explanation: На работе uses 'на' for an idiomatic place (work). Russian categorizes work as a 'на' place, alongside surfaces (на столе) and events (на концерте).

patternRecognition.question: What kind of preposition is being used here?
patternRecognition.explanation: Об Антоне expresses the topic of thinking. The 'б' is added because Антон starts with а (vowel). Об is the variant of о used before vowel-initial nouns.

patternRecognition.question: Which form pattern does Россия follow here?
patternRecognition.explanation: Россия ends in -ия. The prepositional form follows the special pattern: -ия → -ии. So 'в России' (not 'в Россие'). The same applies to лекция → на лекции, история → в истории.

patternRecognition.question: Why does Russian use 'на' here?
options: Стол is a building, so на (exception)
Стол is a surface, so на is correct
patternRecognition.answer: Стол is a surface, so на is correct
patternRecognition.explanation: Стол (table) is a surface, so Russian uses 'на' to express location on it. The case form (-е) follows the standard masculine rule.

reviewVocab.definition: prepositional case (always with a preposition; used for location after в/на and topics after о/об)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Я в Москве' слово 'Москве' стоит в предложном падеже.

reviewVocab.definition: Russia (a -ия noun: the prepositional is России, not Россие)
lecture (another -ия noun: the prepositional is лекции, not лекце)
